item: The columnar opener reports which store it opened: a persisted open that fell back to memory is declined, and an engine that is off is a decline, never built
refs: R268; R269; audit 0.5.0 follow-up; 0.5.1 rollup in-memory fallback misreported as persisted; PR #1518
summary: Two places took a connection for the store that was asked for. (a) columnar.connect returned None only when the engine was off; a persisted open whose encryption gate failed, or whose open raised, fell through to duckdb.connect(':memory:') and returned THAT, indistinguishable from a persisted connection, and _refresh_persisted_build recorded it as the persisted store (_STATE[persisted]=True) and reported built. New columnar.open_store(passphrase, spill, snapshot) returns OpenedStore(con, kind, fallback_reason): kind is persisted, memory or off, fallback_reason a CODE (no-secure-backend, encryption-gate-failed, persisted-open-failed; never the exception's text) set only when a persisted store was asked for and not opened; connect() is a thin wrapper returning .con so its other callers and every stub are unchanged. The kind is reported by the opener, not inferred from the connection. _refresh_persisted_build calls open_store, and when kind is not persisted it CLOSES the store it was handed, records nothing and declines (False, the #1515 decline), with the code in last_skip (why) for the status. When the code is a FALLBACK (encryption-gate-failed, persisted-open-failed) the dispatcher latches the process to the in-memory store, RE-RUNS the start-time verdicts (the stopped hold, the killed-build marker and the affordability check all return None while the persisted store is active, so the first fall-through kick would otherwise have started the in-memory build past the guards the 0.5.0 crash fix put in front of it; the in-build memory guard and the DuckDB limit stop are inside the build and always applied) and builds in memory in the SAME kick if they pass; the latch (_PERSISTED_FELL_BACK, shown in status() as persisted_fallback because a later decline overwrites last_skip; a restart tries the persisted open once more) means the failing open is not retried by every kick and an in-memory stop or failure keeps the in-memory hold the later verdicts read; for no-passphrase, no-secure-backend or engine-off nothing is built for the persisted path (the setting is re-read by the next verdict). (b) REACHABLE TODAY: _build_inmemory_and_swap returned None (= built and swapped in) when connect gave None, and serve_enabled() did not honour OO_COLUMNAR=0 although connect does, so an operator who set OO_COLUMNAR=0 got a serve that built every kick, reported built and had no rollup (answers stayed correct from the live scan). Now serve_enabled() is False under OO_COLUMNAR=0 (forced-on included), and the in-memory build returns an engine-off decline that the dispatcher records as a decline with NO hold (a setting is not a stop). 24 tests in tests/test_rollup_store_kind.py, 2 repointed in tests/test_rollup_persisted_failure_hold.py; red-without by mutation: kind ignored fails 6, no same-kick in-memory build fails 4, no latch fails 4, the fall-through skipping the re-run verdicts fails 3, a verdict error in the re-run keeping a failure hold fails 1, the status not naming the fallback fails 1, a refresh that always declines fails 1, engine-off returning None fails 1, serve_enabled ignoring OO_COLUMNAR fails 1, the gate code dropped fails 1, a persisted store reported as memory fails 1. STATED: the persisted store is dormant in shipped code (blank httpfs pins), so (a) is read from code and exercised through patched gate/attach/opener; (b) is the reachable one. map_serve.serve_enabled had the same OO_COLUMNAR=0 gate gap and is fixed here (one line, one test; R271): its build already returned quietly on a None connection and never claimed a build, so the cost there was a build thread per kick and an enabled status beside a rollup that could not exist. Effect to note: under OO_COLUMNAR=0 card_audit._rollup_gap now returns None (serve_enabled False), so the six trending-scan producers run live in the audit instead of reporting a gap. src/analytics/columnar.py owned for this bundle by R269.
